authors: Lasko, K., Pan, C.G. & Griffin, S.P.
title: Winter tree and terrain shadow correction reveals land cover mapping errors in Sentinel-2 satellite imagery
relevance: Shows that correcting for low-sun-angle TREE and TERRAIN shadow does not merely tidy the imagery - it EXPOSES land cover mapping errors that were previously invisible, i.e. shadow was silently corrupting the map. Directly relevant to our unmeasured illumination axis: acquisitions flown at low solar elevation put large shadows well beyond the actual canopy footprint, which is simultaneously a commission risk (shadow read as dark canopy) and an omission risk (shadowed crowns too dark to detect). Gives the argument for treating sun geometry as a correction step rather than something augmentation absorbs.

authors: Bo, Z.-Y., Lu, W., Chen, H., Chen, S.-B. & Luo, B.
title: SARU: A shadow-aware and removal unified framework for remote sensing images with new benchmarks
source: ISPRS Journal of Photogrammetry and Remote Sensing 239, 39-53
relevance: Current peer-reviewed state of the art for joint shadow DETECTION and REMOVAL on remote sensing imagery, with new benchmarks - the practical tool if we decide illumination must be normalized across our 18 acquisitions. Worth weighing against the cheaper alternative of simply masking shadow to IGNORE rather than reconstructing it, which fits our three-state supervision rule and avoids inventing pixel values the honest-measurement rule would then have to defend. Read as the upper bound on what shadow handling can buy before committing to it.
